paper_metadata.title: OneRel: Joint Entity and Relation Extraction with One Module in One Step
paper_metadata.venue: AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence proceedings copyright notice
paper_metadata.abstract: Joint entity and relation extraction is an essential task in natural language processing and knowledge graph construction. Existing approaches usually decompose the joint extraction task into several basic modules or processing steps to make it easy to conduct. However, such a paradigm ignores the fact that the three elements of a triple are interdependent and indivisible. Therefore, previous joint methods suffer from cascading errors and redundant information. To address these issues, this paper proposes OneRel, a joint entity and relation extraction model that casts joint extraction as a fine-grained triple classification problem. The model consists of a scoring-based classifier and a relation-specific horns tagging strategy. The classifier evaluates whether a token pair and a relation belong to a factual triple, while the tagging strategy supports decoding. Experiments on two widely used datasets report better performance than the state-of-the-art baselines, including on overlapping patterns and multiple triples. evidence:[{

problem_addressed: The paper addresses joint extraction of head entities, relations, and tail entities from unstructured text. It targets cascading errors caused by serial multi-module methods and redundant or incorrectly assembled triples caused by separately recognizing entities and relations. The objective is to identify all triples with one module in one step by classifying token-pair/relation combinations jointly.

methodology.description: OneRel formulates joint extraction as fine-grained triple classification. For every ordered token pair and predefined relation, a scoring-based classifier predicts one of four tags: HB-TB, HB-TE, HE-TE, or -. The model uses BERT token representations, a nonlinear projection of token-pair representations, relation representations, dropout, and softmax classification. Rel-Spec Horns Tagging marks boundary-token combinations for paired head and tail entities. Decoding splices head and tail spans from the boundary tags and reconstructs triples. The score function computes all relation scores for a token pair in parallel. The execution pipeline is: tokenize a sentence; encode tokens with pretrained BERT; enumerate token-pair/relation combinations; score and classify them; obtain the sparse relation-specific tag matrix; decode entity spans and relations from HB-TB, HB-TE, and HE-TE tags; output triples.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: The model uses a predefined relation inventory supplied by each dataset; it does not discover an ontology or construct an ontology. The relation-specific matrix is an internal extraction representation, not an external KG schema.

value: Review-level inference: the method requires a predefined relation set and supervised gold tags, so it does not address ontology discovery or schema adaptation.

Review-level inference: the paper formulates the input as a single sentence and evaluates sentence-level extraction; it does not cover document-level coreference, entity linking, graph fusion, graph validation, or graph updating.
Review-level inference: the scoring tensor has theoretical complexity O(KL²), so cost can increase with relation-inventory size and sentence length.
The reported baselines are taken from prior literature, so cross-method comparisons depend on the compatibility of the cited experimental settings.
